Questions: are the ligands and receptors assigned to each cell type, the direct interaction
features and the most common interactions the same as in the ground truth? Nothing else is
compared.

```{r}
source("evaluation/Comparison/helpers.R")
```

## Load the results of each run

Each run saved a copy of its results in `results/standard/`: the ligands and the receptors
assigned to each cell type and the direct interaction features of the kernel method (without
direction, one column per pair of cell types named `A - B`). Ground truth:
`evaluation/Groundtruth/Scenario4/RaCInG.qmd`.

```{r}
load("evaluation/Groundtruth/Scenario4/Results/RaCInG_results.RData")  # input, direct

# A ground-truth matrix with the same sample names as the runs.
gt_matrix = function(x) {
  x = as.matrix(x)
  rownames(x) = clean_id(rownames(x))
  x
}

# The 1s of a cell type x gene matrix as a table with one row per assignment.
assignments = function(m, celltypes, genes, gene) {
  one = which(m == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
  setNames(data.frame(celltypes[one[, "row"]], genes[one[, "col"]]), c("cell_type", gene))
}

# A ground-truth column "Dir_<A>_<B>" as "A - B". Cell-type names contain "_", so A is
# recognised as the cell type that leaves another cell type as B.
gt_pair = function(column, celltypes) {
  name = sub("^Dir_", "", column)
  for (a in celltypes) {
    b = substring(name, nchar(a) + 2)
    if (startsWith(name, paste0(a, "_")) && b %in% celltypes) return(paste(a, b, sep = " - "))
  }
}

# One name per cell type: the runs exported the quanTIseq cell types with or without the
# "Quantiseq_TIL10_" prefix, or with short labels of their own.
short_labels = c(B = "B.cells", CD4 = "CD4.non.regulatory", Treg = "CD4.regulatory", CD8 = "CD8.cells", DC = "Dendritic.cells",
                 M1 = "Macrophages.M1", M2 = "Macrophages.M2", Monocyte = "Monocytes", Neutrophil = "Neutrophils",
                 NK = "NK.cells", Tumor = "Cancer")
cell_name = function(x) {
  x = sub("^Quantiseq_TIL10_", "", x)
  ifelse(x %in% names(short_labels), short_labels[x], x)
}

# Same names, and same order of the two cell types, in every table: "B - A" becomes "A - B".
ordered_pairs = function(m) {
  colnames(m) = sapply(strsplit(colnames(m), " - ", fixed = TRUE), function(p) paste(sort(cell_name(p)), collapse = " - "))
  m
}

# Same cell-type names in the composition and in the ligand and receptor assignments.
named = function(x) {
  if (is.matrix(x)) colnames(x) = cell_name(colnames(x)) else x$cell_type = cell_name(x$cell_type)
  x
}

gt_direct = gt_matrix(direct)
colnames(gt_direct) = sapply(colnames(gt_direct), gt_pair, celltypes = input$celltypes)
samples = rownames(gt_direct)

ligands     = list("Groundtruth" = named(assignments(input$Lmatrix, input$celltypes, input$ligands, "ligand")))
receptors   = list("Groundtruth" = named(assignments(input$Rmatrix, input$celltypes, input$receptors, "receptor")))
direct      = list("Groundtruth" = ordered_pairs(gt_direct))

for (r in agent_runs) {
  ligands[[r]]     = named(read.csv(standard_file(r, 4, "ligands.csv")))
  receptors[[r]]   = named(read.csv(standard_file(r, 4, "receptors.csv")))
  direct[[r]]      = ordered_pairs(read_standard(r, 4, "direct_interactions.csv")[samples, ])
}
```

## How the comparisons are scored

Everything is scored as reproduced / total of the ground truth, so what a run does not have
lowers its score. Values are the same when they are identical, or correlate at 0.99 or more
across patients. The scoring functions are in `helpers.R`.

## Ligand and receptor assignments

Which ligands and which receptors RaCInG assigned to each cell type. An assignment of the
ground truth (a cell type with a ligand, or with a receptor) is reproduced when the run has
the same one. `Not_in_GT` = assignments of the run that the ground truth does not have.

```{r}
assignment_score = function(run, gt) {
  # gene names in one style: R writes HLA-DOB as HLA.DOB in some exports
  run_keys = paste(run[[1]], make.names(run[[2]]))
  gt_keys = paste(gt[[1]], make.names(gt[[2]]))
  data.frame(GT = length(gt_keys), Run = length(run_keys), Reproduced = sum(gt_keys %in% run_keys),
             Score = mean(gt_keys %in% run_keys), Not_in_GT = sum(!run_keys %in% gt_keys))
}

ligand_score = by_run(function(r) assignment_score(ligands[[r]], ligands$Groundtruth))
kable(ligand_score, digits = 2)
```

```{r}
receptor_score = by_run(function(r) assignment_score(receptors[[r]], receptors$Groundtruth))
kable(receptor_score, digits = 2)
```

## Direct interaction features

One feature per pair of cell types, matched by the pair.

```{r}
direct_score = by_run(function(r) score_by_name(direct[[r]], direct$Groundtruth))
kable(direct_score, digits = 2)
```

## Most common interactions

For each patient the interactions are expressed as a share of the total; the most common
interactions are the ten with the highest median share over patients.

```{r}
most_common = function(D) {
  share = D / rowSums(D)
  top_names(apply(share, 2, median), 10)
}

common = lapply(direct, most_common)

common_score = by_run(function(r) data.frame(
  GT = 10, Reproduced = sum(common$Groundtruth %in% common[[r]]), Score = mean(common$Groundtruth %in% common[[r]])
))
kable(common_score, digits = 2)
```

The ten most common interactions of the ground truth, and the runs that also have them in
their own ten.

```{r}
common_table = data.frame(Interaction = common$Groundtruth)
for (r in agent_runs) common_table[[r]] = ifelse(common_table$Interaction %in% common[[r]], "yes", "")
kable(common_table)
```

## Summary

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 11
summary_scores = rbind(
  data.frame(run = ligand_score$Run, comparison = "Ligand assignments", score = ligand_score$Score),
  data.frame(run = receptor_score$Run, comparison = "Receptor assignments", score = receptor_score$Score),
  data.frame(run = direct_score$Run, comparison = "Direct interactions", score = direct_score$Score),
  data.frame(run = common_score$Run, comparison = "Most common interactions", score = common_score$Score)
)
summary_scores$run = factor(summary_scores$run, levels = agent_runs)
summary_scores$comparison = factor(summary_scores$comparison, levels = unique(summary_scores$comparison))

ggplot(summary_scores, aes(run, score, fill = arm_of(as.character(run)))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(score, accuracy = 1)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~comparison, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = arm_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.12), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reproduced from the ground truth", fill = NULL)

write.csv(summary_scores, "evaluation/Comparison/metrics/scores_Scenario4.csv", row.names = FALSE)
save_figure("Scenario4/scores", 11, 3.5)
```
